summary: The University of Manchester's Global Futures Scholarships for Africa take £12,000 a year off international tuition fees for three years of a bachelor's, or £19,000 off a master's, for self-funded students from listed African countries, Ghana and Nigeria among them, who start in September 2027. Selection is on academic merit. Bachelor's applicants need A-levels, the IB or a recognised foundation year, not WASSCE alone.
meta_title: Manchester Global Futures Scholarships for Africa 2027
meta_description: Manchester takes £12,000 a year off bachelor's fees, or £19,000 off a master's, for self-funded students from Ghana and other African countries in 2027.
covers: Bachelor's: £12,000 off international tuition fees in the first year, and £12,000 in each of the second and third years if you reach 60% in each year's final exams and assessments, up to £36,000.
Master's: £19,000 off the published overseas tuition fee for a full-time, on-campus master's.
Both are fee discounts; living costs are not included.
eligibility: Bachelor's: students who lived mainly in Botswana, Ghana, Kenya, Mauritius, Nigeria, South Africa or Zimbabwe for the last three years, taking A-levels, the IB, South Africa's NSC or IEB Matric, the NCUK International Foundation Year or the Bridge House College Foundation.

Master's: students from Botswana, Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa or Zimbabwe whose bachelor's degree is from Africa, with an unconditional offer for a full-time, on-campus master's starting in September 2027.
You must be self-funded, not sponsored.
Selection is mainly on academic merit, from your grades and the online application form.
how_to_apply: Bachelor's: apply to Manchester through UCAS. After you receive an offer, the university emails you the scholarship form, from December 2026.
Return it by 25 February 2027 in round 1 (students who sat their final exams in 2026) or by 8 April 2027 in round 2, and make Manchester your UCAS Firm choice by 15 May 2027.
Master's: hold an unconditional offer and complete the online scholarship form by 20 April 2027; results come by 24 May 2027.
Bachelor's results come by 2 April 2027 (round 1) or 12 May 2027 (round 2).
watch_out: WASSCE alone does not meet Manchester's bachelor's entry requirements: WASSCE holders first complete a University-recognised foundation programme.
The award covers part of the fee, not all of it, so you still need the rest of the fee and your living costs.
Bachelor's awards exclude Medicine (MBChB), Dentistry (BDS), Architecture, courses with an integrated foundation year and anyone who has studied in the UK before.
Master's awards exclude the MBA, MPhil, MArch, PGCE, clinical medicine and dentistry, and anyone whose bachelor's degree is from outside Africa.
costs: UK Student visa and the Immigration Health Surcharge
documents: A UCAS application (bachelor's) or a Manchester master's application, leading to an offer
The Global Futures online scholarship form
Results or predicted grades in A-levels, the IB, NSC or IEB, or the NCUK or Bridge House foundation (bachelor's)

faq.q: Can Ghanaian students get the Manchester Global Futures Scholarship?
faq.a: Yes. Ghana is on both the bachelor's and the master's list for Africa, for September 2027 entry.

faq.q: Can I use it for nursing?
faq.a: Nursing is not on the excluded list, which names only Medicine, Dentistry, Architecture and courses with an integrated foundation year.

Not directly for a bachelor's. Manchester asks WASSCE holders to complete a recognised foundation programme first, and the scholarship accepts the NCUK International Foundation Year or the Bridge House College Foundation.
